research_question: How far is a newly discovered specimen of Indotyphlops braminus in Tlaxcala, Mexico from the nearest previously known occurrence in GBIF?

phase_1.user_prompt: I've just found what appears to be a Brahminy blindsnake (Indotyphlops braminus) in Tlaxcala, Mexico. I want to check all known occurrences of this species in Mexico to see if this represents a new state record or a range extension. Can you help me find the relevant occurrence data?

phase_2.user_prompt: Please download all the occurrence records for the Brahminy blindsnake in Mexico. I need the geographic coordinates so we can map them.

phase_3.user_prompt: I collected my new specimen at latitude 19.323583 and longitude -98.243333. Please process the downloaded GBIF data to ensure all records have valid coordinates, and then calculate the straight-line (Haversine) distance from my new observation to every other existing record in Mexico.

phase_4.user_prompt: Find the minimum distance to the nearest previously recorded Brahminy blindsnake from my location. Also, create a map showing my new record as a distinct marker (e.g., a red star) alongside the downloaded GBIF records as background points to visualize the distribution. Save the map as `new_record_map.png`.

checkpoint.reference_conclusion: The new specimen represents a new record for the state of Tlaxcala, located approximately 26 km in a straight line from the nearest previously known GBIF record in the neighboring municipality of Puebla.
checkpoint.visual_description: A map of central Mexico showing GBIF occurrence points for Indotyphlops braminus, with a distinct, highlighted marker (like a star) at coordinates (19.323, -98.243) representing the new observation.
